gist: US death row inmate Christa Pike is unconscious after a failed lethal injection execution.
Lawyers claim prison officials botched the execution by failing to insert IV lines correctly.
Tennessee's governor ordered an independent review and halted all executions for the year.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: US death row inmate Christa Pike is unconscious and on a ventilator following a failed execution attempt. Her lawyers filed an emergency motion to preserve evidence, alleging prison officials botched the lethal injection. They state officials used at least seven needles, bending one, while Pike whimpered and cried. An expert suggested the drug pentobarbital entered tissue under her skin rather than her bloodstream due to ruptured veins or blood clots.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Tennessee Governor Bill Lee has halted all executions in the state for the year and ordered an independent review. Pike's lawyers had previously warned that her blood-clotting condition and small veins risked causing unnecessary pain.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Authorities have not yet said whether they will attempt to execute Pike again, and her lawyers are seeking to preserve all physical, written, and electronic evidence.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The victory could test Canadian unity. Plamondon has pledged to hold an independence referendum and challenge the federal government on immigration. He also plans to abolish Quebec's ties to the monarchy, which could trigger legal battles. However, polls suggest only 30% of Quebecers support independence.

sections.heading: What happens next

stories.standfirst: Altering molecular handedness has implications for the origins of life.

articles.title: Chemistry Nobel goes to reactions like those that gave life a hand
articles.standfirst: Altering molecular handedness has implications for the origins of life.

timeline.text: Chemistry Nobel goes to reactions like those that gave life a hand

gist: Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai won the Chemistry Nobel for biased chiral reactions.
Their discoveries explain how chemical reactions can produce excesses of single molecular forms.
This research has practical applications for pharmaceuticals and implications for origin-of-life studies.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for discovering chemical reactions that produce large excesses of one chiral form of a molecule. Kagan showed that a chiral catalyst could drive reactions favoring a single chirality. Soai found reactions where a product acted as a catalyst to boost the same reaction, turning a tiny initial excess into over 99 percent of a single form.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Life relies on molecules with specific handedness, or chirality, and key enzymes fail to work with the wrong form. Finding new ways to catalyze specific chiral forms helps address challenges in origin-of-life research. It also has immense practical utility for producing pharmaceuticals, as wrong chiral forms in drugs can be inactive or harmful.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Women accounted for approximately a quarter of new hires in artificial intelligence roles over the past year, and just thirteen percent in executive positions. Meanwhile, women are overrepresented in roles exposed to AI disruption such as customer service. Across all AI occupations, men hold a higher median pay, and women are disproportionately concentrated in low-paying jobs like data annotators.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Advocates warn that this trend could create the greatest gender pay gap in generations. It risks leaving women out of building foundational technology and transforming a participation gap into a power gap.

sections.heading: What happens next

gist: Spanish pensioner Maricarmen Abascal has died following her eviction from her Madrid flat.
Her eviction ignited nationwide protests, encampments and widespread anger over Spain's housing crisis.
The political fallout caused failed housing reforms and triggered an early general election.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Eighty-seven-year-old Maricarmen Abascal died in hospital two weeks after being removed on a stretcher from her Madrid home of over seven decades. The flat's owner had significantly raised her rent, which exceeded her pension. Although the firm later offered a return agreement, Abascal died before signing. Her eviction sparked mass demonstrations across Spain.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Abascal became a national symbol of the housing crisis. Tens of thousands protested, setting up encampments in Madrid and other cities. The outrage triggered major political instability when parliament rejected emergency housing legislation. Consequently, Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called a snap general election for 29 November, seeking a broader progressive majority to overcome conservative resistance.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Unions have scheduled a general strike for 11 November. Parliament's permanent council will vote on two newly approved cabinet housing decrees containing 21 measures. Meanwhile, Spain heads to the polls on 29 November, with opinion polls suggesting the conservatives are likely to finish as the largest party.

fivew: Evicted 87-year-old pensioner Maricarmen Abascal died in hospital.
Her death was announced two weeks after her 23 September eviction.
She died in hospital in Madrid, Spain.
She suffered severe exhaustion after being evicted over unaffordable rent increases.

gist: Pioneering computer scientist Margaret Hamilton has died at the age of 90.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Computer pioneer Margaret Hamilton has died aged 90, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology announced. The Guardian reported she died on 30 September, while Ars Technica noted she died last week. Hamilton learned programming at MIT, worked on weather simulations and air defence projects, and became the first programmer and first woman hired by MIT's Instrumentation Lab for Nasa's Apollo programme. In 2016, President Barack Obama presented her with the nation's highest civilian honour, which the BBC called the Presidential Medal of Honor and other outlets identified as the Presidential Medal of Freedom.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Hamilton coined the term software engineering and directed the Apollo onboard flight software development. During the 1969 Apollo 11 moon landing, her software's failsafe mechanisms compensated for computer overloads, averting an abort and allowing the Eagle module to land safely.

gist: French finance minister Roland Lescure invited the UK to rejoin the European Union.

Burnham warned that planned EU manufacturing rules could damage British industry and supply chains.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: French finance minister Roland Lescure has invited the UK to rejoin the European Union. His comments followed statements by Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who suggested a second Brexit referendum was possible. Burnham stated that Brexit had caused "more harm than good" and proposed exploring options including rejoining the customs union, the single market, or full EU membership.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Burnham warned that the EU's planned "Made In Europe" scheme, designed to protect EU industry from Chinese competitors, could damage British industry and supply chains. Lescure responded that if the UK rejoined, it would have a seat at the table to discuss these rules. Meanwhile, Reform UK leader Nigel Farage argued that reviving the Brexit debate would boost his party.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Burnham is travelling to Germany for talks with Chancellor Friedrich Merz to discuss closer security cooperation and UK-EU relations.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Netflix has released Below, a six-part supernatural thriller set in the struggling Newfoundland fishing community of Snook's Arm. A scientist, played by Mackenzie Davis, discovers the mass is actually a giant frozen mucous membrane. This snot-berg was created by a massive squid, which was released by thawing Arctic permafrost and has begun killing people.

sections.heading: Why it matters

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Researchers found that watching a "People's Emergency Briefing" film significantly increased viewers' motivation to act on climate and nature breakdown. A survey of 13,000 viewers showed that 93% felt the public is not being fully informed about these crises.

sections.text: Professor Lorraine Whitmarsh noted that while people know some climate risks, secondary risks like food security and national security are less obvious. gist: Major national and global shocks have caused a lasting decline in UK mental health.
The Brexit referendum and the first Covid lockdown caused the most significant psychological distress.
Heightened distress has persisted, leaving NHS mental health services struggling to cope with demand.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A study found that five major shocks since 2016, including Brexit and the first Covid lockdown, caused a lasting decline in UK mental health. Other shocks included the Ukraine invasion, the second lockdown, and Liz Truss's mini-budget.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The research shows that major government decisions and global events seriously damage mental wellbeing. The resulting psychological distress has persisted, contributing to record numbers of people being too sick to work and NHS services struggling to cope with a near-doubling of patients since 2016.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Human Rights Watch reports that the US has deported over 500 migrants to African countries where they are not citizens. These individuals, who have no prior connection to the destination nations, allegedly face arbitrary detention, ill-treatment, and the risk of being sent back to countries where they fear persecution. sections.heading: Why it matters

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Startup Goodfire released a monitoring system for AI agents that observes internal model signals. Unlike traditional methods that require a secondary AI to review output, this approach uses small detectors called probes to read calculations already being performed. The technology is currently available to customers of Baseten.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Existing monitoring methods are often expensive and slow because they involve re-reading text. Goodfire claims its method is significantly cheaper and faster, as it reuses existing computations. This is intended to help secure open models, which developers may strip of safeguards, by providing guardrails during inference.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: South Korea announced it will recall its ambassador to Ukraine following a diplomatic dispute. The row began after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that two captured North Korean soldiers had been transferred to Seoul. South Korea stated Ukraine broke an agreement to keep the transfer secret, while Zelensky's office maintained no such non-disclosure agreement existed.

sections.text: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung faced domestic criticism over the revelation, with the opposition accusing him of wanting to cover up the transfer. sections.text: South Korea stated it will continue consultations with the Ukrainian side and expects outstanding issues to be resolved smoothly. Meanwhile, Ukrainian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Heorhii Tykhyi stated that Ukraine remains open to restoring a constructive dialogue.

sections.text: Asos told customers that hackers accessed detailed profiles of potentially millions of users, after BBC News informed the retailer of contact from the cyber criminals. The stolen data includes names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, dates of birth, and website search histories. Hackers, calling themselves Xuanyewen, reportedly gained access by impersonating a trusted contact to obtain an employee's login credentials.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The risk of impersonation scams and convincing phishing attacks has increased. Although Asos stated that no bank details or passwords were stolen, a victim expressed worry that the data could be used for future attacks.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Asos is investigating the breach and will contact customers if further action is needed. Experts advise users to remain highly suspicious of unsolicited messages and to change passwords as a precaution.

gist: The US government has blocked Microsoft and other tech firms from a foreign worker program.
Vice President JD Vance accused Microsoft of abusing visas to replace American workers.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The US government has suspended Microsoft and seven other technology firms, including Adobe, from a program that helps foreign workers obtain permanent US residency. Vice President JD Vance accused the companies of abusing the H-1B visa system to replace American workers with cheaper foreign labour. The Department of Labor announced it will not process new or pending applications from these firms.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Vance claimed Microsoft laid off American workers while filing thousands of visa applications, undercutting domestic wages. Microsoft rejected these allegations, stating that eighty per cent of its H-1B filings were for existing employees rather than new hires, and that its international staff receive the same compensation as US workers. Immigration advocacy groups argue that attracting global talent benefits the US economy, while Vance described the visa recipients as "indentured servants".

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Microsoft plans to provide the US administration with additional information regarding its hiring practices. Meanwhile, the US government has proposed eliminating the sixty-day grace period for laid-off visa holders.

articles.title: Will El Niño and the polar vortex bring snow to the UK this winter?

timeline.text: Will El Niño and the polar vortex bring snow to the UK this winter?

gist: El Niño is growing and influences weather globally.
Late winter impacts might include a disrupted polar vortex.
UK snow and ice remain far from guaranteed.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A strong El Niño event is developing in the Pacific Ocean and releasing heat into the atmosphere. This climate phenomenon affects weather patterns worldwide and increases the probability of wet and stormy conditions during the UK autumn. In the late winter period, energy from El Niño can travel upwards to disrupt the polar vortex.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: A disrupted polar vortex can raise the probability of cold weather, ice and snow in the UK. Past winters show mixed evidence as some El Niño years brought extreme cold while others remained very warm, and major cold snaps occurred during different climate phases.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Current forecasts indicate that significant cold weather or snow is not likely in the near future for the UK.

fivew: El Niño is growing and may influence UK winter weather patterns.

gist: More women report feeling daily anger, driven by unpaid work and everyday sexism.
Cultural media depictions increasingly present female rage as understandable and liberating.
Experts suggest harnessing anger mindfully and authentically rather than suppressing it.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: An increasing number of women in the UK and globally are reporting daily anger, breaking away from historical expectations to remain polite and hide frustration. This shift is mirrored in popular culture, where female rage is increasingly depicted as understandable and liberating rather than unstable.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Women continue to shoulder a heavier burden of unpaid work and the mental load compared to men, alongside ongoing threats of violence, sexism, and harassment. While suppressing anger can lead to physical conditions, women expressing anger at work can still face social penalties.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Experts suggest women can harness their anger as a messenger to protect boundaries and confront injustices. Coaches advise using direct language and mindfulness strategies like the RAIN method to channel anger effectively without causing harm.

timeline.text: Running out of royals: why calls are growing to let Japan’s princess Aiko take the throne

gist: Calls are growing in Japan to allow Princess Aiko to take the throne.
A 140-year-old law forbids women from ascending to the Chrysanthemum throne.
Conservative government changes safeguard male-only succession despite strong public support for change.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Princess Aiko is the popular only child of Emperor Naruhito and Empress Masako. Under a long-standing law, women cannot ascend to the throne. Recent amendments backed by the government of Sanae Takaichi safeguard male-only succession by allowing women to retain royal status after marriage and resurrecting male-line descendants from collateral branches.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The imperial family is shrinking, leaving very few male heirs in the line of succession. Opinion polls show strong public support for a female emperor to avert a looming succession crisis, but conservative leaders insist on maintaining the male-line tradition.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Amendments safeguarding male-only succession go into effect later this month, but public unease and Aiko's popularity may continue to fuel the debate over female emperors.

fivew: Princess Aiko, Emperor Naruhito, and Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi.
A looming succession crisis driven by a shrinking royal family clashes with public support for a female emperor.

quotes.text: The unparalleled historic fact that the imperial line has been maintained through the male line for 126 generations is the foundation of the emperor’s authority and legitimacy.

It is important for society to keep progressing ... I believe the duty of the imperial family is to act in response to the requests of society ... I do not think there are any differences between women and men.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: An ICE agent shot and injured an undocumented Dominican man in the Bronx, New York, on Thursday. Reports indicate agents surrounded the man and a five-year-old child in a car before firing. The child was unharmed. DHS said the officer discharged his weapon during an operation, alleging the man had prior convictions and gang associations.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The shooting sparked protests and clashes with police outside the hospital where the man was taken. Local officials condemned the incident, with New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani calling it unconscionable and demanding an end to ICE actions.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Mayor Mamdani plans to ask US President Donald Trump to end ICE operations in the city. Immigration advocates have called for an independent investigation and the prosecution of the officer.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Criminal gangs dumped nearly 40,000 tonnes of waste in Hoads Wood, Kent, over six months in 2023. The Environment Agency-led clean-up took 15 months and cost taxpayers £15m.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The site is an ancient woodland and a Site of Special Scientific Interest. Conservationists say it will take decades for ancient woodland species to return to the damaged area.

sections.heading: What happens next

gist: Peter Greenaway's assisted dying drama starring Dustin Hoffman is stuck in post-production hell.

The film, originally called Lucca Mortis, faces an ongoing row over rights and distribution.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Filming began in Lucca, Tuscany, in late 2023 after initial cashflow delays. The production faced further issues when producers made a separate, more commercial cut without the director, citing budget overruns. Two unfinished versions now circulate while rights remain contested.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The stalemate leaves the legacy project for Peter Greenaway and Dustin Hoffman in limbo. Local authorities in Lucca, who supported the production enthusiastically, are disappointed by the prolonged silence and lack of release.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The film remains stuck in post-production purgatory, raising doubts over whether distributors and festivals will accept a version without the director's final say.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Anti-immigration protests in Soweto and Durban turned violent, resulting in 24 vehicles being set ablaze, foreign-owned shops looted, and buildings attacked. sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The violence highlights deep-seated tensions over immigration, poverty, and unemployment. The unrest was triggered by anger over a Constitutional Court ruling enabling undocumented arrivals to apply for asylum, which officials say led to false claims and overwhelming queues.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The government stated it will change how it complies with the court ruling while still abiding by it. Authorities promised to pursue those responsible for the destruction.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A masked gang of at least seven people stole 30,000 bottles of prestigious wine, worth €5m, from the Marchesi Antinori winery in Tuscany. The thieves deactivated alarms, disabled cameras, and used company forklifts to load two trucks on Saturday. The theft was discovered on Monday morning.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: This is the largest wine theft of its kind in Italy. The stolen bottles, including prized Tignanello and Solaia reds, are highly valued. Outlets disagree on the price per bottle, reporting ranges of €150 to €500 or €120 to €400. The winery's insurance does not cover the loss.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Investigators are searching for the stolen wine, with hopes that road cameras will help trace the trucks. The winery has warned customers to beware of any offers outside official channels.

timeline.text: Alison Hammond: 'I thought I was having heart attack on air'

gist: Presenter Alison Hammond feared she was having a heart attack during a live broadcast.
She rushed off air and was hospitalised, but had suffered a panic attack.
Hammond returned to the show a week later to discuss her experience.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: During a live broadcast of ITV's This Morning last Friday, presenter Alison Hammond rushed off air after experiencing what she feared was a heart attack. She was taken to hospital, where tests revealed she had actually suffered a panic attack. Hammond described the experience as "very real" and one of the scariest things she had ever been through.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The incident highlighted the intense pressure of presenting live television. Returning to the show a week later, Hammond and psychologist Dr Sian Williams discussed panic attacks to raise awareness. Williams explained that panic attacks represent "anxiety on overdrive" and can feel identical to heart attacks due to shared physical symptoms like chest pain.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Hammond has returned to her regular presenting slot on This Morning. She noted that the health scare has given her a new perspective, prompting her to take stock of her health.

fivew: She suffered a panic attack on air that she mistook for a heart attack.
The incident occurred last Friday, and she returned to the show this Friday.
The event took place live on the ITV programme This Morning.

gist: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor surrendered his Royal Lodge lease, leaving a £1.5m repair bill.
King Charles paid the repair costs to protect the Crown Estate from financial loss.
Royal Lodge will be marketed commercially, with no plans for another royal occupant.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor surrendered his lease on Royal Lodge, incurring dilapidation and repair charges. Deducting £302,000 in early departure compensation left £1.5m owed to the landlord. The King covered this settlement using private funds, though The Times reported that he contributed to the repair costs.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The King intervened to ensure the Crown Estate was not left out of pocket. Mountbatten-Windsor had previously relocated to Sandringham amid controversy surrounding his ties to Jeffrey Epstein. While his upkeep is funded by the King, his brother will not finance his legal battles over police search warrants.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Royal Lodge will be marketed commercially by two recognised agents to provide returns for the nation, with no plans for another royal resident.

fivew: King Charles paid repair costs for Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor.
A £1.5m repair bill on Royal Lodge was settled.
The lease officially ended in October.
The property is located at Royal Lodge in Windsor.
The payment was made to avoid leaving the Crown Estate out of pocket.

quotes.text: The lease for Royal Lodge has ended and our focus now is firmly on its future use and the opportunities to generate additional financial value for the nation from its early return

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The Trump administration has imposed new financial sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC). The measures block ICC assets in US jurisdictions and ban US entities from conducting transactions with the court, giving them six months to wind down business.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated the sanctions defend US sovereignty against a court trying to prosecute Americans. The US also objects to ICC actions against Israeli officials. Conversely, the ICC called the sanctions an attempt to obstruct justice and an assault on the international legal order.

sections.heading: What happens next

sections.text: Mikhail Zvinchuk, founder of the Rybar war blog, was arrested in Montenegro alongside four other Russian citizens. Police and security agents detained the group on suspicion of spreading Russian influence. Local reports indicated they faced expulsion on national security grounds.

gist: Four Conservative candidates have declared their run for the London mayoral nomination.
The Conservative Party has only won the London mayoralty once in 26 years.
The final shortlist of two candidates is expected to be announced in November.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Four Conservative candidates have declared their bids to run for London mayor in the May 2028 election. The declared runners are Sir James Cleverly, Festus Akinbusoye, Andrew Boff, and Alex Challoner.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The Conservatives have only won the London mayoralty once in 26 years, with Boris Johnson. Since then, they have lost three consecutive elections to Labour's Sadiq Khan. However, the party hopes to regain ground following local election victories in Westminster and Wandsworth in May 2026.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The hopefuls must wait until November to see if they make the final shortlist. London party members are expected to choose between the final two candidates, who will likely be announced on 20 November.

gist: Family calls for allergy ratings after a girl died from an unwashed blender.
A cafe and its proprietor were fined following a fatal allergic reaction.
Food safety officials emphasise that businesses must take allergen risks seriously.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A 12-year-old girl died of anaphylactic shock after drinking a milkshake from a south-east London cafe. The blender used had not been washed after making a previous drink containing tree nuts. The cafe and its proprietor were subsequently fined after admitting charges related to food safety.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The family argue that current food hygiene ratings do not inform consumers about a business's allergy management systems. They are campaigning for a dedicated allergy rating scheme so people with food allergies can make safer choices.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The Food Standards Agency states it is keeping its policy under review and has produced new guidance and training for businesses regarding allergen responsibilities.

gist: Liverpool's academy uses strict rules, like car engine limits, to keep young players grounded.
The club is adapting its wage structure to navigate a distorted youth transfer market.
A planned twenty million pound facility revamp aims to boost future player development.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Liverpool's academy director, Alex Inglethorpe, outlined the club's youth development approach, which includes strict rules on phones and car engine sizes to encourage humility.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Brexit and rising competition have distorted the market for 16-year-old players, prompting Liverpool to review its academy wage structure. Additionally, recent departures like Trent Alexander-Arnold and Curtis Jones have left the first team without local-born players.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The club plans a £20 million revamp of its academy facilities by 2028 to continue producing elite talent under new sporting director Julian Ward.

gist: Jon Rahm is leaving LIV Golf after finding LIV 2.0 terms unacceptable.
LIV Golf filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy after losing Saudi funding.
Rahm tops the list of creditors with an unsecured claim of $7.5m.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Jon Rahm is set to leave LIV Golf because he considers the terms of LIV 2.0 unacceptable. LIV Golf filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in the United States in September following the withdrawal of Saudi Arabia's funding. The league has secured possible financing from BC Partners Credit for the 2027 season. Rahm and LIV representatives are in advanced discussions for a consensual separation agreement.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Rahm is owed an unsecured claim of $7.5m, making him the top creditor among the 30 largest unsecured claims. Participants are owed at least $45m and can leave, as players have no obligation to sign on to LIV 2.0.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Talks are open until 25 October, and it is hoped that a consensual separation agreement will be finalised by a court hearing on 5 November.

Why is JJ Gabriel in Man Utd's team photo?

gist: JJ Gabriel features in Manchester United's official team photo despite efforts to leave.
Europe's top clubs are interested in the teenager as he holds a European Union passport.
His decision to seek a move was triggered by non-inclusion against Sabah FK.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: JJ Gabriel is included in Manchester United's official team photo for the season. The pictures were taken before he informed the club of his intention to leave. His exit decision was triggered by not being included in the squad to face Sabah FK.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Gabriel is a target for several top European clubs, including Real Madrid and Barcelona. Manchester United hold his registration and would consider legal action if illegal inducement emerges.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Gabriel is set to turn 16 and his next involvement in a United game will virtually certainly be as an opposition player.
